primary_source_search_status: identified_via_search_snippets, body not readable: op-ed by Prof. Havi Dreifuss (Tel Aviv University / Yad Vashem; chair of the International Treblinka Council appointed by Poland's Culture Ministry), replying to Prof. Daniel Blatman's Haaretz op-ed of 2026-09-24 ('ושוב צריך להזכיר להיסטוריונים ה"מודאגים": מוזאון טרבלינקה אינו סניף של יד ושם', https://www.haaretz.co.il/opinions/2026-09-24/ty-article-opinion/.premium/000001a0-d3ab-d9ab-abfd-f7ab23e70000). Background: Haaretz feature 2026-09-22 'A Catholicization of Treblinka?' (https://www.haaretz.com/jewish/2026-09-22/ty-article-magazine/.premium/a-catholicization-of-treblinka-polands-renovation-alarms-historians/000001a0-be62-d310-a9bf-bfea75130000) and the Treblinka Museum's response 'Treblinka: Memory and Responsibility towards the Historical Record' (https://muzeumtreblinka.eu/en/2026/09/22/treblinka-memory-and-responsibility-towards-the-historical-record/); Polish coverage at dzieje.pl, zero.pl, kultura.wp.pl. Both op-eds are .premium and haaretz.co.il is egress-blocked; only the search-engine teaser of the Dreifuss piece was visible (it argues Blatman frames an Israeli-vs-Polish conflict, whereas the real divide is documentation-based vs politically driven commemoration).
claims_note: No judgable data claim identified: the headline and the only visible teaser text are editorial framing ('research vs political distortion', 'not Israeli-Polish'), which is out of scope per the auditable-claim scope rule. The slug's 'victim count' premise is not borne out — the 2026 dispute is about commemoration (Jedwabne/Radziłów name stones, ~300 crosses at Treblinka I, the Jan Maletka plaque, the Black Road, the planned permanent exhibition), not the victim total; the museum itself cites 800,000-900,000 Jews murdered at Treblinka II, consistent with the scholarly range (~780,000-925,000), and no party in the coverage found contests that figure. Factual sub-issues in the wider debate (e.g. that Jedwabne's and Radziłów's Jews were murdered in the July 1941 local pogroms, not deported to Treblinka — which the museum's own 2026-09-22 statement concedes) could not be attributed to this op-ed's text because the body is unreadable, so none were scored.

context_reference_figures.jedwabne_pogrom: 10 July 1941, roughly 300-1,600 Jews murdered by local Poles (estimates vary; JHI cites ~1,000 in some summaries)
